name: Blue to Purple Progression
description: A study-planning guide for blue belts using Stephan Kesting’s positional categories and the IBJJF graduation rules.
summary: Organize what you can explain from top and bottom, then separate study priorities from promotion eligibility.
overview: When your notes contain many techniques but leave some positions blank, an inventory can make the next study choice clearer. Kesting’s Sample Technique List separates submissions, top transitions and bottom transitions. Use those categories to organize your existing learning. Belt recognition is a separate question addressed by the IBJJF graduation rules and your professor.

guide.display_title: Blue to Purple: Build a Study Inventory

fits: You are a blue belt with scattered technique notes and want a specific subject to bring to your next coaching conversation.
consider_alternative_if: If your immediate goal is a tournament, Competition Strategy narrows the inventory to the options you intend to use at that event.

includes: A way to compare your own top, bottom and submission notes against a published positional map.
The distinction between an instructor’s promotion decision and IBJJF recognition requirements.
limits: The technique list is illustrative; it is not a purple-belt examination.
No fixed number of guards, tournaments or training months establishes readiness for promotion.

start_here.title: Find a gap in the same position from opposite roles
start_here.task: Open the Sample Technique List and select a position you encounter often. Sort your own notes into its top-transition, bottom-transition and submission categories. Mark a category you cannot yet explain and take that specific gap to your instructor. Use Article 3 separately if you need to check belt-recognition eligibility.
start_here.section: Kesting: Sample Technique List, printed pages 29–30. IBJJF graduation: Article 3.

sources.title: A Roadmap for Brazilian Jiu-jitsu — Stephan Kesting
sources.note: Read the Sample Technique List and its explanation of organizing an individual repertoire. Kesting explicitly presents examples rather than an exhaustive curriculum.

sources.title: IBJJF General System of Graduation
sources.note: Read Article 3: recognition depends on applicable minimum periods and exceptions; promotion timing remains at the professor’s discretion. These are recognition rules, not a technical syllabus.

flashcards.question: Does completing an IBJJF minimum belt period automatically entitle a student to promotion?
flashcards.answer: No. Article 3.2.2 leaves promotion timing to the professor while requiring applicable minimum periods for IBJJF recognition.
